I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t be forgetting. And sometimes I’ll go to do a repair job and show up without the right tools, which is embarrassing because I used to be pretty good about that. I’ll have the whole thing in my head, then somehow leave the one thing I needed sitting at home.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel your forgetfulness is clearly worse now than it was 10 years ago?\n\nPatient: I think… yeah, probably. It’s hard to say “clearly,” because I’ve always been a little scattered, but now it’s stuff I really shouldn’t be missing. Like heart follow-up appointments, or I’ll tell myself I need to call the clinic back and then—gone, it just slips away.\n\nAnd with repair jobs, I’ll show up without the right tool, which drives me nuts. I used to keep a better handle on that sort of thing.
